does: Cuts a vegetable into equal halves with one clean cut, usually lengthways through the stem, so that each half lies flat and can be roasted, scooped or filled.

intro.what: One clean cut splits a vegetable into equal halves that lie flat.
intro.why: Halves cook evenly and make a boat for a filling.

how: Lay the vegetable on a board and steady it with your flat hand on top.
Cut down through the middle from end to end with a large sharp knife, through the stem if it has one.
Lay the halves cut side up. Score the flesh or scoop it out if the dish asks for it.

cues.text: The halves are the same size and lie flat without rocking.

mistakes.mistake: Sawing at the vegetable, which tears the flesh and gives uneven halves.
mistakes.fix: Use a large, sharp knife and one long cut.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting off the stem, so that the halves fall apart when filled.
mistakes.fix: Leave the stem on and cut through it.

quiz.question: Why cut through the stem and leave it on?
choices: It holds each half together as it cooks and is filled.
quiz.because: The stem keeps the halves whole.

quiz.question: What makes a good half for filling?
choices: A small piece cut from the side.
A half that lies flat and matches the other.
A half with the skin peeled off.
quiz.because: Even halves cook in the same time and hold a filling.
